text.p: Gold plunged to a new 2-1/2 year low under heavy selling overnight. Gold has been under pressure from institutional and producer selling for several days, and several traders said they were betting on it to fall to $370.

A late rally by copper dragged other base metals from their lows but base metals failed to reach last week's peaks. Crude oil futures prices were pressured by news that Bagdad has agreed to all conditions for the oil-for-food deal with the United Nations. The CRB index was down 0.76 at 243.43

Gold fell sharply in New York trading for the third day. COMEX gold futures posted fresh life-of-contract lows in every delivery month out to December 1997 during the session. "It remains a market under pressure," North American Equity Services floor trader, John Geraghty said. "Lease rates are up and the funds remain heavily net short, but there's still a possibility of a short covering bounce, ahead of the Thanksgiving Day holiday Thursday and Friday this week." COMEX December gold closed down $1.80 at $374.50 an ounce after seeing a new contract low at $373.40. Spot bullion market was quoted in late trade $374.25/374.75 compared to the London Monday fix at $375.40 and the Friday New York close at $376.10/376.60.

A late rally in London Metal Exchange (LME) copper prices lifted the other base metals by Monday's close, though several traders believed prices would now consolidate ahead of Tuesday's all important stock data. Benchmark three months delivery copper was last at $2,204, against Friday's LME kerb close of $2,187.
The cash to three months backwardation after narrowing in to $145 earlier flared to settle at $170.
Traders noted a move by the London Clearing House (LCH) to raise copper's cash to three months spread margin. The LCH said the spread margin was raised to $3,750 from $1,875.
This action should deter fundamental tightness from being further exacerbated by speculative activity. "It will help to prevent a speculative accumulation on top," one source said.
Eyes will again fall on the inventories on Tuesday which are likely to show a small fall. But several traders suggest that copper stocks could start to rise over the coming weeks.

This could help to cap any potential spikes in the market against the backdrop of speculative liquidation, though, substantial deliveries into LME warehouses will be needed to seriously dent the market. Traders will closely watch movements of stocks into LME Singapore and Long Beach warehouses.

Elsewhere aluminium, in line with copper, moved away from support at $1,500 to settle at $1,513, versus Friday's $1,504.50. It continued to be underpinned by nearby tightness though traders noted a lack of strong physical interest.
Nickel gained $30 to $6,940. LME stocks are expected to rise on Tuesday. Lead was $4 higher at $709, while zinc settled at $1,082, up $3.

OIL - NYMEX crude continued to be pressured Monday by news Iraq agreed to terms of the oil-oil-for-food deal, but selling was contained as some of the deal's impact was already priced into the market, traders said. "The big question is how much of this is factored into the marketplace. We started to see a a fall Wednesday and last Friday toward the close," said Gerald Samuels, managing director at ARB Oil. January crude stood 26 cents lower at $23.49 a barrel at the close.
GRAINS - Wheat closed 5-1/4 to 1/2 cent per bushel higher on the Chicago Board of Trade on short covering and commercial buying but gains were limited by late selling by some major trading houses.
